messages:
alex.k: Heads up — NimbusHealth reported 503s and 429s to the hosted endpoint backed by their dedicated pool nh-reserved-prod since 10:12 UTC. They say it started right after a marketing campaign spike. Can someone take point? :eyes:

maya_s: Is this the pool that was configured with min=4 / max=8 nodes? any baseline/peak qps numbers from the customer?

alex.k: Yep config is min_nodes=4, max_nodes=8. Customer reports baseline ~45 qps sustained, peak bursts up to ~520 qps for ~2-3 minutes. They expected the autoscaler to handle it.

josh_support: Pasting the kube/autoscale events we got from the telemetry (truncated):

```
10:11:58 UTC - scale_up triggered (from 4 -> 5) reason: queued_requests > 50
10:12:10 UTC - scale_up triggered (from 5 -> 6)
10:12:32 UTC - scale_up cooldown prevented further scaling (cooldown=180s)
10:13:05 UTC - pod OOM on node-3 (model worker oom) => 503s
10:13:20 UTC - rate limit 429 seen on fronting router due to global token bucket exhaustion
```

josh_support: Also seeing p95 latency climb from 120ms -> 1.2s during the spike, queue depth spiked to ~220.

mike_runtime: Autoscaler config note: step_policy=1 node per scale_up, cooldown=180s. That means if bursts are faster than the cooldown we can't add more than 1 node every 3 minutes. For short spikes (2-3 minutes) this underprovisions.

mike_runtime: Quick recommendation: change scaling step to 2 and cooldown to 60s for this pool as a short-term mitigation. Also increase max_nodes to 10 to give more headroom.

liam_sre: We also observed one tenant on the same pool (noisy-tenant-42) running a large batched eval job concurrently — GPU mem pressure peaked and caused OOMs which killed worker pods. That's likely the 503 root cause, not just autoscale lag.

maya_s: If it's noisy neighbor + slow scale, that explains both 503s (workers dying) and 429s (front router token bucket exhausted while queueing).

amy_acct: Nimbus is asking for a predictable SLA for campaign windows. They want guidance on baseline sizing vs burst headroom, and an emergency step we can take today.

tina_oncall: Short-term runbook for support ops: 
1) Temporarily set pool max_nodes=10 and scale_step=2, cooldown=60s.
2) Evict noisy-tenant-42 from nh-reserved-prod (move to shared-burst or throttle their jobs).
3) Enable burst_capacity=true for the pool (allows short OS-level overcommit).
4) If 503s persist, apply immediate model fallback route to a smaller variant (gpt-small) for the campaign route.

alex.k: Repro steps for load test (run from staging to mimic customer):
```
# simple vegeta-style loop (adjust concurrency to simulate peak)
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.company/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","input":"hello","max_tokens":16}' &
done
```

mike_runtime: Also add a headroom target to autoscaler: aim for 50% GPU util as target so we don't push to 90% during normal peaks. That maps to a sizing rule: required_nodes = ceil(requested_qps / (capacity_per_node * 0.5)).

liam_sre: Long-term fixes: a) Tenant isolation (move heavy batch jobs to separate pools or schedule off-peak), b) autoscaler fast-path for burst detection (detect sudden ramp and temporarily bypass cooldown), c) graceful pod preemption to avoid OOM kills.

amy_acct: I'll flag a billing/order option: reserved burst addon (guaranteed extra nodes for N hours) and offer Nimbus a one-time credit for this outage.

alex.k: I've started the changes Tina suggested (max_nodes=10, cooldown=60s, step=2) and evicted noisy-tenant-42. Will monitor.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0458 — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0458 (assigned to eng-runtime) :rotating_light:

josh_support: After the quick config change we see p95 drop back to ~160ms and queue depth down to ~30. Customer confirmed errors stopped at 10:26 UTC.

maya_s: Follow-up action items:
- Mike: open PR to add burst-aware scale policy + reduce default cooldown for reserved pools (RFC).
- Liam: propose tenant isolation heuristics and enforcement for dedicated pools.
- Amy: scope commercial reserved-burst offering and pricing.
- Alex/Josh: run a replay test for Nimbus campaign throughput and write a postmortem with timeline.

alex.k: Thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and ping Nimbus with the immediate mitigations and offer for the reserved-burst add-on. :white_check_mark:
